messages:
Valerie: Heads-up — customer (acme-corp) just flagged their Insights dashboard showing rows from other orgs. Screenshot + sample row pasted. :eyes:
Alex: I can repro on prod - querying the insights endpoint for their org returns ~2% rows where org_id is null or points to other orgs. Quick dump: `items[42].org_id == null`
Mike: Ugh. Any recent deploys to insights/prefetch?
Sana: We rolled out enable-insight-prefetch-v2 to 25% at 09:07 UTC, ramping to 50% at 11:00. That rollout touched the route that merges cached previews across user sessions.
Alex: repro steps (minimal):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/insights?org_id=54321&limit=50" 
# response contains rows with "org_id": null and one with "org_id": 9988
```
Mike: That smells like a cache-key bug: prefetch service might be omitting org_id when computing keys for the preview cache. If it merges a global cached response into a per-org result set we leak rows.
Valerie: Is this only previews or full queries as well? Customer says the saved view shows other customers' snippets in widgets.
Alex: So far seen in both Insights preview queries and the saved view hydrate path. The hydrate uses the same preview cache layer for speed.
Ivy: deploy-bot: deploy insight-prefetch-v2 finished at 10:59 UTC to 50% (build 2026.3.18-824) :information_source:
deploy-bot: rollouts: feature enable-insight-prefetch-v2 -> 50%
Sana: Confirmed the rollout included a template change that switched cache key composition in prefetch/cache actor. I pushed the change.
Mike: Let's mitigate: pause the rollout (set to 0%) and invalidate the preview cache for affected clusters. Any objections?
Valerie: Do it. Customer impact > perf improvement. @Sana can you pause the flag?
Sana: On it. Pausing now... done. Flag set to 0% on prod. :white_check_mark:
Alex: Kicking a cache invalidation job for preview namespace on prod region us-west-2. Job id: cache-inv-17355.
Mike: Also put an emergency canary rollback on the deploy pipeline — revert the prefetch template change. Can someone open a quick PR to revert?
Valerie: Alex — can you revert and trigger a canary rollback? I'll notify support and security.
Alex: Opening revert PR now, will attach CI and request canary rollback to 0->100 revert path. (PR: revert-insight-prefetch-key-17355)
Ivy: quick note: I see tracing spans with x-org-id header empty for some preview fetches at 10:51-10:58. Possibly client header mapping bug upstream too.
Mike: Good catch. We need to check both: 1) cache key composition, 2) whether any upstream proxy can drop x-org-id for preview calls.
Sana: I'll audit the prefetch actor change; if it relied on `context.org?.id` maybe we had an edge case for anonymous previews.
Valerie: Action items:
- Alex: revert prefetch template + trigger canary rollback (now).
- Alex: invalidate preview cache (job started).
- Mike: add unit/regression test that ensures cache keys include org_id and user scope.
- Sana: audit commit + confirm whether header mapping could be lost.
- Valerie: notify affected customer + escalate to security if we confirm cross-org exposure.
Alex: Revert PR submitted and rolling back canary now. Patch will be in prod within 7m if CI passes.
Sana: Found root cause: cacheKey = join([route, queryHash, userScope]) — previous code used userScope which can be empty for saved prefetch; the new change accidentally dropped org id from userScope when profile was incomplete. Fix in review to include fallback to org_id.
Valerie: Good. After rollback, let's do a quick runbook entry for this class of bug + a dashboard alert for anomalous cross-org row counts.
Ivy: I'll add a tracing alert for empty x-org-id on preview fetches and a metric for percent of rows with org_id != request_org_id.
Mike: Nice. Once rollback finishes, do a manual sweep on customer dataset and confirm no remaining leaks.
Valerie: Thanks all — keep this thread updated. I've pinged support and legal just in case. :thumbsup:
